GLib 0.18.5 — VFang compatibility/security backport

Upstream source: crates.io glib 0.18.5
Archive: https://static.crates.io/crates/glib/glib-0.18.5.crate
Archive SHA-256:
233daaf6e83ae6a12a52055f568f9d7cf4671dabb78ff9560ab6da230ce00ee5
Original COPYRIGHT and MIT LICENSE are retained.

The only change to upstream source is the two-line out-pointer mutability
correction in src/variant_iter.rs. It is the exact fix in gtk-rs PR #1343:
https://github.com/gtk-rs/gtk-rs-core/pull/1343
Merge commit: 05dff0ee696f9bcd8617cd48c4b812d046d440cb
Advisory: https://rustsec.org/advisories/RUSTSEC-2024-0429.html

VariantStrIter::impl_get now declares a mutable pointer and passes &mut p to
g_variant_get_child. Previously C wrote through an immutable Rust reference,
which is undefined behavior and can produce a null-pointer crash in optimized
builds. The binding API and dependency versions are unchanged.

The Tauri manifest patches crates.io glib to this local source. GTK, GIO,
WebKitGTK and other dependencies resolve to this same patched crate; replacing
only VFang's direct GLib usage would not fix their binding implementation.

The optimized regression in ../../vendor-tests/glib-regression tests borrowed
string-array iteration through next, next_back, nth, nth_back and last,
including Unicode and an empty string. It requires only GLib development
libraries and opens no window. Linux CI runs it separately from Tauri tests.

The upstream package version stays 0.18.5 for compatibility. Version-only
advisory scanners may still flag RUSTSEC-2024-0429; validate this source patch
and regression instead of representing the upstream version as fixed or
suppressing all GLib advisories. Transitive maintenance warnings remain.

When upgrading GTK/Tauri, check whether a compatible fixed upstream binding
can replace this vendor copy. Keep this backport and its optimized regression
until the entire GTK dependency graph uses a fixed binding. Do not modify
generated upstream bindings or broaden this patch without an upstream source
reference and focused validation.
